The channel-assignment invariant is correctly implemented. `eta_int_modulator()` returns a scalar in {1.00, 0.85, 0.70, 0.60}. It is consumed by the R_k pipeline as a multiplicative factor on η_int:

```
η_int_modulated = m · η_int
η_combined = η_int_modulated · (1 − c_ext · (1 − ν_k))
q = η_combined · d · p
R_k(i) = R_k(i-1) · (1 − q) / (1 − q · R_k(i-1))
```

The function takes a `DivergenceRecord` and returns a `float`. It has no access to R_k, no access to ν_k, no access to q. It cannot pre-multiply R_k because it never sees R_k. It cannot credit ν_k because it never reads or writes ν_k. The orthogonality contract is enforced structurally — by API surface, not by runtime assertion. This is the strongest form of the invariant: violation requires changing the function signature, not just the logic.
